repositories.name: agent-desktop
repositories.description: Computer use CLI for AI agents
repositories.readme:
# agent-desktop Computer use for AI agents: see and operate desktop apps on macOS, Windows, and Linux through the OS accessibility tree.

agent-desktop gives an AI agent computer use without screenshots or pixel matching. It reads the accessibility tree of a desktop app and returns it as JSON, with a ref for every element the agent can act on. The agent clicks or types on a ref, reads the UI again to check the result, and repeats. The loop lives in your agent; agent-desktop has no model inside. It ships as a CLI and a C library. Snapshots, clipboard reads, screenshots, command output, and debug artifacts can contain private desktop content. Keep them out of public logs and uploads. ## Install ```bash npm install -g agent-desktop agent-desktop status # platform, permissions, supported surfaces agent-desktop permissions --guide # macOS: walks you through the Accessibility grant ``` Bun, Yarn and pnpm can install the same package. It includes native binaries and platform helpers for x64 and ARM64. For direct execution without a JavaScript launcher, download the matching native archive from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop/releases) and keep its helper beside the executable. On macOS and Linux, Homebrew also works: `brew install agent-desktop`. There is no official Scoop package yet. The repository no longer maintains a custom Homebrew tap or Scoop bucket. Release archives and building from source are covered in [Installation](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/installation). ## Quick start ```bash agent-desktop snapshot --app Finder -i # interactive elements, each with a ref agent-desktop click @s8f3k2p9:e8 # act on a ref from that snapshot agent-desktop snapshot --app Finder -i # observe again to verify ``` Each command prints one JSON envelope. A trimmed snapshot: ```json { "version": "2.6", "ok": true, "command": "snapshot", "data": { "app": "Finder", "snapshot_id": "s8f3k2p9", "ref_count": 59, "complete": true, "tree": { "role": "window", "name": "Downloads", "children": [ { "role": "treeitem", "name": "Documents", "ref_id": "@s8f3k2p9:e8", "available_actions": ["Click"] } ] } } } ``` - **Refs belong to their snapshot.** A bare `@e8` is rejected with `INVALID_ARGS`. When the UI changes, an action returns `STALE_REF` or `AMBIGUOUS_TARGET`: take a new snapshot and use its refs. - **Several windows** give `AMBIGUOUS_TARGET`; `snapshot` lists the candidate window ids in `error.details`. Pass one with `--window-id`. - **Dense apps:** map first with `snapshot --skeleton --app Slack -i --compact`, then drill into one region with `snapshot --root @s8f3k2p9:e3 -i --compact`. - **Headless by default.** Ref actions use the accessibility API without moving the pointer or taking focus. The global `--headed` flag allows physical input. - **Post-action waits** observe the ref's original process. Window-owned refs stay pinned to their original window, including refs captured from a sheet, alert, popover, focused view, or Linux menu. macOS application menus keep their application-owned surface and need no document window. The wait reads the whole pinned window, so overlay selectors share its scope. [Wait scope and results](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/configuration#post-action-wait-flags) describe the selector limits. - `type`, `set-value`, and `clipboard-set` accept `--stdin` for piped text, keeping it out of process arguments. Run secret steps as separate commands; batch JSON text appears in process arguments. - **PowerShell.** Quote every ref (`'@s8f3k2p9:e8'`), because a bare `@token` is the splatting operator. The full walkthrough is in the [quick start](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/quick-start). ## How it works Your agent calls the CLI, or the C library in process. Both run the same core, which reaches the OS only through `PlatformAdapter`. Each binary is built for one OS and talks to that OS's accessibility API. ## For AI agents The binary carries guides that match its version: ```bash agent-desktop skills get desktop # the loop, refs, verification and retry rules agent-desktop skills get platform # what differs on the OS you run on agent-desktop --help # flags for one command ``` Install the skill into an agent harness from [skills.sh](https://skills.sh/vercel-labs/agent-desktop/agent-desktop): ```bash npx skills add https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-desktop --skill agent-desktop ``` Or add this to your `AGENTS.md`: ```markdown Use `agent-desktop` to see and operate desktop apps. Before the first use, run `agent-desktop skills get desktop` and `agent-desktop skills get platform`, and follow them. ``` Retry a failed command only when `error.disposition.retry` is `safe`. See [JSON output](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/json-output) for the envelope, error codes, and exit codes. ### MCP `agent-desktop mcp` serves every command as an MCP tool over stdio. A tool is named after its command (`desktop_snapshot`, `desktop_click`, `desktop_session_start`), takes that command's arguments, and returns its JSON envelope: ```json { "mcpServers": { "agent-desktop": { "command": "agent-desktop", "args": ["mcp"] } } } ``` Global flags given to `mcp`, such as `--session`, `--headed` or `--trace`, apply to every call. ## Commands agent-desktop has 60 command names, 56 operational commands. The other four (`key-down`, `key-up`, `mouse-down`, `mouse-up`) refuse to run until a daemon can release a held key or button. [Commands](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/commands) documents each one. | Group | Commands | |---|---| | Observe | `snapshot`, `find`, `get`, `is`, `screenshot`, `list-surfaces` | | Act on a ref | `click`, `double-click`, `triple-click`, `right-click`, `type`, `set-value`, `clear`, `focus`, `select`, `toggle`, `check`, `uncheck`, `expand`, `collapse`, `scroll`, `scroll-to` | | Keyboard and mouse | `press`, `hover`, `drag`, `mouse-move`, `mouse-click`, `mouse-wheel`, `key-down`, `key-up`, `mouse-down`, `mouse-up` | | Apps and windows | `launch`, `close-app`, `list-apps`, `list-windows`, `list-displays`, `focus-window`, `resize-window`, `move-window`, `minimize`, `maximize`, `restore`, `open-system-surface` | | Notifications | `list-notifications`, `dismiss-notification`, `dismiss-all-notifications`, `notification-action` | | Clipboard | `clipboard-get`, `clipboard-set`, `clipboard-clear` | | Wait | `wait` | | Sessions | `session`, `trace`, `cursor-overlay` | | System | `status`, `permissions`, `version`, `batch`, `skills` | ## Platform support | Platform | Requirement | Accessibility API | |---|---|---| | [macOS](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/platforms/macos) | macOS 13 or later, Intel or Apple Silicon | AX API | | [Windows](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/platforms/windows) | Windows 10 1809 or later, x64 or ARM64 | UI Automation | | [Linux](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/platforms/linux) | Ubuntu 24.04 or later, x86_64 or aarch64, X11 or Wayland | AT-SPI | Each platform page lists what works headless, what needs `--headed`, and what refuses. ## C library Each release ships `libagent_desktop_ffi`, so a program can call agent-desktop in process. See the [C library docs](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/ffi). ```python import ctypes lib = ctypes.CDLL("./lib/libagent_desktop_ffi.dylib") lib.ad_adapter_create.restype = ctypes.c_void_p lib.ad_adapter_destroy.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p] assert lib.ad_init(7) == 0 # AD_RESULT_OK when the header's AD_ABI_VERSION_MAJOR matches the library adapter = lib.ad_adapter_create() lib.ad_adapter_destroy(adapter) ``` ## Development Each platform adapter builds only on its own OS, so scope cargo to the host's packages. On macOS: ```bash HOST_PKGS=(-p agent-desktop-core -p agent-desktop-macos -p agent-desktop -p agent-desktop-ffi) cargo test "${HOST_PKGS[@]}" cargo clippy "${HOST_PKGS[@]}" --all-targets -- -D warnings ``` On Windows, use `agent-desktop-windows` instead of `agent-desktop-macos`; on Linux, `agent-desktop-linux`. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) lists every gate. ## Documentation - [Introduction](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop): what it is and how it works - [Snapshots and refs](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/snapshots-and-refs) - [Errors and recovery](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/errors-and-recovery) - [Skills](https://agent-browser.dev/desktop/skills) - [CONCEPTS.md](CONCEPTS.md): vocabulary - [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md), [SUPPORT.md](SUPPORT.md) ## License Apache-2.0

repositories.name: t3code
repositories.readme:
# T3 Code

T3 Code is an "agent harness control surface". It enables control of the agents on your machine with a best-in-class mobile app ([iOS](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/t3-code-remote-claude-more/id6787819824), [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.t3tools.t3code)), [web app](https://app.t3.codes) and [Electron-based desktop app](https://t3.codes).

Works with your subscriptions on Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, and fx. If they're set up on your computer, T3 Code can control them.

## "Wait, what are you selling me?"

Nothing. We built T3 Code because we wanted the best possible development experience with agents. We were inspired by existing solutions like the Codex desktop app, Conductor, Claude Desktop and Cursor Glass, but none met our bar.

We wanted something performant, remote-ready, and truly open. If we ever go the wrong direction, we want you to have everything you need to fork and build the editor that you want.

## Installation

> [!WARNING]
> T3 Code currently supports Codex, Claude, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, Antigravity, and fx. Install and authenticate at least one provider before use:
>
> - Codex: install [Codex CLI](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli) and run `codex login`
> - Claude: install [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code) and run `claude auth login`
> - Cursor: install [Cursor CLI](https://cursor.com/cli) and run `agent login`
> - Grok Build: install [Grok Build CLI](https://x.ai/cli) and run `grok login`
> - OpenCode: install [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) and run `opencode auth login`
> - Antigravity: enable it in Settings, then use **Install Antigravity** and **Sign in with Google**. No CLI is required.
> - fx: install [fx](https://fx.sh) and run `fx login` on the machine running the T3 Code server ([setup guide](./docs/user/providers-fx.md))

### Command line

```bash
curl -fsSL https://t3.codes/install.sh | sh
```

On Windows, in PowerShell:

```powershell
irm https://t3.codes/install.ps1 | iex
```

Then run `t3` to start the server and open the local web app. `t3 service install` keeps it running in the background, `t3 update` moves to a newer release, and `t3 --help` has the full reference.

To try it once without installing, run `npx t3@latest` instead.

### Desktop app

Install the latest version of the desktop app from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/releases), or from your favorite package registry:

#### Windows (`winget`)

```bash
winget install T3Tools.T3Code
```

#### Windows (`scoop`)

```bash
scoop install extras/t3code
```

#### macOS (Homebrew)

```bash
brew install --cask t3-code
```

#### Debian, Ubuntu (`.deb`)

Download the `.deb` from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/releases), then:

```bash
sudo apt install ./T3-Code-*.deb
```

#### Arch Linux (AUR)

Stable:

```bash
yay -S t3code-bin
```

Nightly:

```bash
yay -S t3code-nightly-bin
```

The AUR packaging is maintained in this repository under [`packaging/aur`](./packaging/aur).

#### Nix (nixpkgs)

```bash
nix profile add github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable#t3code
```

The package is maintained in [nixpkgs](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/tree/nixos-unstable/pkgs/by-name/t3/t3code)
and includes the desktop app (`t3code-desktop`) and the `t3` command.
See [Nix installation](./docs/user/install.md#nix-nixpkgs) for NixOS configuration and updates.

## Some notes

We are very very early in this project. Expect bugs.

We are (mostly) not accepting contributions yet. Small fixes may be considered. Big features will not be.

## Documentation

Full docs live in [docs/](./docs). There's no docs site yet.

- [FAQ](./docs/user/faq.md)
- [Install and first run](./docs/user/install.md)
- [Permission modes](./docs/user/permission-modes.md)
- [Keyboard shortcuts](./docs/user/keybindings.md)
- [Project settings](./docs/user/project-settings.md)
- [Appearance preferences](./docs/user/appearance.md)
- [Remote access from a phone or another machine](./docs/user/remote-access.md)
- [Connect Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT and other agents over MCP](./docs/user/outside-agents.md)
- [Keeping app and server in sync](./docs/user/updating.md)
- [Source control integrations](./docs/user/source-control.md)
- Multiple accounts: [Codex](./docs/user/providers-codex.md) · [Claude](./docs/user/providers-claude.md)
- [Run T3 Code as a background service](./docs/user/background-service.md)

Building from source? Start at [docs/internals/overview.md](./docs/internals/overview.md).

## If you REALLY want to contribute still.... read this first

### Install `vp`

T3 Code uses Vite+ so you'll need to install the global `vp` command-line tool.

#### macOS / Linux

```bash
curl -fsSL https://vite.plus | bash
```

#### Windows

```bash
irm https://vite.plus/ps1 | iex
```

Checkout their getting started guide for more information: https://viteplus.dev/guide/

### Install dependencies

```bash
vp i
```

Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) before reporting a bug or opening a PR.

Have a feature request? Start an [Ideas discussion](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/discussions/categories/ideas).

Need support? Join the [Discord](https://discord.gg/jn4EGJjrvv).

repositories.name: impeccable
repositories.description: The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with polish and bolder, review with critique and audit, catch AI slop before it ships.
repositories.readme:
# Impeccable The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with `polish` and `bolder`, review with `critique` and `audit`, and catch AI slop before it ships. From your project root: ```bash npx impeccable install ``` Reload your coding tool, then run `/impeccable init` in your agent (`$impeccable init` on Codex). Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Replit Agent, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, Kiro, Trae, Rovo Dev, Qoder, Mistral Vibe, Pi, Hermes Agent, DeepSeek Harness, and Veto. Full docs live at [impeccable.style/docs](https://impeccable.style/docs). | Without Impeccable | With Impeccable | |---|---| | ![Villa Castagneto built without Impeccable: cream background, a thin serif headline with an italic accent, two pill buttons, and flat vector illustrations in rounded cards](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/raw/main/docs/images/readme-without.webp) | ![Villa Castagneto built with Impeccable: a full-bleed engraved night scene of the villa on its cliff above the sea, a condensed cream and vermilion headline, and a month strip along the bottom](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/raw/main/docs/images/readme-with.webp) | Same model (Fable 5.1), same brief: a fourteen-room family guesthouse on the Ligurian coast. Without Impeccable, it builds the tasteful default: cream page, thin serif, italic accent, pill buttons. With it, the page is built around one picture: the house at night, seen from the water. For a full project, see the [Neo Mirai case study](https://impeccable.style/cases/neo-mirai): a conference site taken from mockup to shipped page. ## Why Inter for everything. Purple-to-blue gradients. Cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds, a rounded-square icon tile above every heading. Ask an agent for a page with no other guidance and these show up again and again, across models and projects. - **Words for what you want.** "Make it pop" leaves your agent to guess. `/impeccable bolder the pricing cards` loads a playbook written for that one move and points it at one target. - **A reviewer.** `critique` scores the design against usability heuristics and ranks what to fix first. `audit` checks accessibility, performance, theming, and responsive behavior, with findings ranked P0 (blocking) to P3 (polish). - **A slop detector.** 62 deterministic rules flag the tells above, plus quality problems like cramped padding and skipped headings. No LLM, no API key. Impeccable is strongest on interfaces that already exist: point it at a page or a component and iterate. It builds new pages too; see [Build something new](https://impeccable.style/docs/new-work) for how to get the most out of that harder mode. To start, pick one component: ``` /impeccable critique the pricing cards ``` ## How it works Run `/impeccable init` once per project. It reads your code, asks only what it can't infer (who the product is for, what it needs to do, the constraints), and writes `PRODUCT.md`. Every later command reads it. Run `/impeccable document` to capture your existing visual system in `DESIGN.md`, so changes stay on-brand. [More on context files](https://impeccable.style/docs/context). Then name a command and a target: ``` /impeccable critique the onboarding flow /impeccable quieter the landing page /impeccable polish settings /impeccable harden checkout ``` Or just describe what you want: `/impeccable redo this hero section`. Narrow targets get better results; a single section reviewed closely beats a whole page at a glance. Pin a command you use often with `/impeccable pin audit` to get `/audit` as its own shortcut. ### 24 commands | | Commands | |---|---| | **Steer** | `bolder` amplifies safe designs · `quieter` tones down loud ones · `distill` removes what the page doesn't need · `colorize` brings color to a gray interface · `typeset` fixes fonts, hierarchy, and sizing · `layout` fixes spacing and rhythm · `animate` adds transitions and interaction feedback · `delight` adds personality · `overdrive` goes for shaders, spring physics, and scroll-driven effects | | **Review** | `critique` is a scored UX review · `audit` is a technical quality report | | **Finish** | `polish` is the final pass before shipping · `harden` covers errors, i18n, overflow, and edge cases · `clarify` rewrites unclear copy · `adapt` handles screen sizes and devices · `optimize` fixes loading and rendering performance · `onboard` designs first-run flows and empty states | | **Iterate live** | `live` lets you pick an element in the browser and cycle through variants · `generate` produces variants of a named element without manual picking | | **Plan and set up** | `shape` plans UX before code · `init` writes `PRODUCT.md` · `document` writes `DESIGN.md` · `extract` pulls repeated patterns into your design system | The 24th, `craft`, is a deprecated alias for a plain build request. Type `/impeccable` alone to see the list in your agent. Each command has its own page: [impeccable.style/docs](https://impeccable.style/docs). On Codex, open `/skills` or type `$impeccable` instead of the slash command. ### Live mode `/impeccable live` opens your running dev server with an overlay. Select an element, pick a direction, and Impeccable hot-swaps variants in place. Accept one and it is written back to your source. It works with Vite, Next, SvelteKit, Astro, Nuxt, and plain HTML. [Iterate in the browser](https://impeccable.style/tutorials/iterate-live). Live mode edits a local checkout only; don't inject it into a deployed site or weaken a production CSP to make it work. Applying copy edits runs your `package.json`'s optional `impeccable:manual-edit-validate` script with your permissions, so review it before using live mode in an unfamiliar repo. Apply sends staged copy edits to your chat agent while a live session is polling. If none has polled in the last minute, it runs the `codex` CLI from your PATH instead (or `claude` when codex is missing), with approvals, permission checks, and sandboxing off (`--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` or `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`) and your environment inherited. Its prompt carries the staged edits, the edited elements' HTML and nearby text, the page URL, and candidate source paths. Set `IMPECCABLE_LIVE_COPY_AGENT=chat` in the environment that starts live mode to keep Apply in your chat session, or `off` to disable Apply. The server reads it once at startup. ## Three ways to run the detector **In your agent.** The design hook scans every UI file your agent edits and hands the findings back before the agent calls the work done. This is where most slop gets caught: without the hook, the detector only runs when someone remembers to run it. It's available on Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, and Hermes Agent, and the installer sets it up. Say yes. [Automatic design checks](https://impeccable.style/docs/hooks). **In CI or your terminal.** The CLI needs no agent: ```bash npx impeccable detect src/ # scan a directory npx impeccable detect https://example.com # scan a rendered page (uses your installed Chrome or Edge) npx impeccable detect --json . # machine-readable output npx impeccable detect --github src/ # GitHub Actions annotations npx impeccable detect --list-rules # every rule with its id and description ``` Source files like JSX and TSX get the pattern rules only. Rules that need a rendered page, such as low contrast and tiny text, run when you scan a URL, so point the CLI at your dev server too: `npx impeccable detect http://localhost:5173`. Exit code `2` means findings, `1` means a target couldn't be scanned. To allow your brand font everywhere, run `npx impeccable ignores add-value overused-font Inter --reason "Brand font"`. To turn a rule off for one file, add a comment: ``. [Run a detector scan](https://impeccable.style/docs/detector) · [Configuration and ignores](https://impeccable.style/docs/config). **In your browser.** The [Chrome extension](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/impeccable/bdkgmiklpdmaojlpflclinlofgjfpabf) overlays the same findings on any live page, yours or anyone else's. [Review with a visual overlay](https://impeccable.style/tutorials/critique-with-overlay). ## Installation ```bash npx impeccable install ``` The installer detects your coding tools, asks whether to install for this project or globally, and offers the design hook where your tool supports one. Accept the hook. Reload your tool afterward. `npx impeccable update` refreshes an existing install. For scripts, pass `--providers=claude,codex,cursor` and `--scope=project|global`. Three tools need one more step before the hook runs. In Codex, open `/hooks` and approve the project hook (again after an update that changes it). In Grok Build, run `/hooks-trust` or launch with `--trust`. In Hermes Agent, the hook is a plugin: run `hermes plugins enable impeccable-design-hook` once. [Allow the hook in your harness](https://impeccable.style/docs/hooks#allow-the-hook-in-your-harness). Node is only needed for `npx`. The skill itself runs a self-contained engine binary that ships next to it or downloads once into `~/.impeccable/bin/`.
Claude Code, Copilot, and Grok plugins **Claude Code:** `/plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable`, then open `/plugin` and install Impeccable. **GitHub Copilot in VS Code:** install [Impeccable from the Visual Studio Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=renaissance-geek.impeccable) or run `code --install-extension renaissance-geek.impeccable`. Needs VS Code 1.109.3+, Copilot Chat, and a trusted workspace. It installs the skill without the hook. [Details](docs/VSCODE-EXTENSION.md). **Grok Build:** `grok plugin install pbakaus/impeccable#plugin --trust` installs the skill, agents, and hook.
Git submodule (a pinned version for the whole team) ```bash git submodule add https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable vendor/impeccable npx impeccable link --source=vendor/impeccable --providers=claude,cursor ``` Commit `.gitmodules`, the submodule, and the generated links. Teammates run `git submodule update --init --recursive`. To upgrade, run `git submodule update --remote vendor/impeccable`, rerun the `link` command, and commit. Linking installs skills, not hooks. Existing skill folders stay put unless you pass `--force`.
Manual copy, no Node required Download the ZIP for your tool from [impeccable.style](https://impeccable.style), or clone this repo: each tool's build is committed at the repo root. Copy `skills/impeccable` from the folder below into the same place in your project, or into the global folder. | Tool | Repo folder | Global skills folder | |---|---|---| | Claude Code | `.claude/` | `~/.claude/skills/` | | Cursor | `.cursor/` | | | Codex CLI, Replit Agent | `.agents/` | `~/.agents/skills/` | | Devin | `.devin/` | `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/devin/skills/` | | GitHub Copilot | `.github/` | | | Gemini CLI | `.gemini/` | | | Google Antigravity | `.agent/` | `~/.gemini/config/skills/` | | OpenCode | `.opencode/` | | | Grok Build | `.grok/` | `~/.grok/skills/` | | Hermes Agent | `.hermes/` | `${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/` | | DeepSeek Harness | `.dsh/` | `${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/` | | Pi | `.pi/` | | | Qoder | `.qoder/` | `~/.qoder/skills/` | | Rovo Dev | `.rovodev/` | `~/.rovodev/skills/` | | Mistral Vibe | `.vibe/` | `~/.vibe/skills/` | | Trae | `.trae/` | `~/.trae/skills/` | | Trae China | `.trae-cn/` | `~/.trae-cn/skills/` | For example: `mkdir -p your-project/.claude/skills && cp -r .claude/skills/impeccable your-project/.claude/skills/`. Notes: - A manual copy skips the design hook and subagents. Run `npx impeccable install` to get them; it writes each tool's hook pointing at the right skill path. - OpenCode also needs `.opencode/commands/impeccable.md` copied into your project's `.opencode/commands/` to provide `/impeccable`. - Hermes asks you to trust project-local skills once: run `hermes skills trust` from the project root. Global installs need no trust step. - Cursor and Gemini CLI may need Agent Skills enabled in settings. See the [Cursor](https://cursor.com/docs/context/skills) and [Gemini CLI](https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/skills/) skills docs. - Restart Trae after copying. - `impeccable install` and `update` manage a DeepSeek Harness global copy only when `DSH_HOME` is inside your home directory.
## Project files and git Impeccable writes its working files under `.impeccable/`. A few are shared project artifacts and belong in the repo: `config.json`, `live/config.json`, `design.json`, `surfaces/*.md`, and `critique/*.md`. Keep `PRODUCT.md` and `DESIGN.md` in the repo too. The rest is screenshots, caches, and runtime state.
Copy the .gitignore entries ```gitignore # impeccable-ignore-start # Ephemeral output, runtime state, and per-dev overrides. # The **/ prefix covers .impeccable at the repo root or in a nested workspace. # Shared artifacts stay tracked: config.json, live/config.json, # design.json, surfaces/*.md, critique/*.md. **/.impeccable/config.local.json **/.impeccable/hook.cache.json **/.impeccable/hook.pending.json **/.impeccable/*.png **/.impeccable/review/ **/.impeccable/questions/ **/.impeccable/live/server.json **/.impeccable/live/sessions/ **/.impeccable/live/previews/ **/.impeccable/live/annotations/ **/.impeccable/live/cache/ **/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-apply-transaction.json **/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-events.jsonl **/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-evidence/ **/.impeccable/live/pending-manual-edits.json **/.impeccable/live/deferred-svelte-component-accepts.json **/.impeccable/live/*.png # impeccable-ignore-end ```
The folders that hold decision-round state (`.impeccable/questions/`, `.impeccable/mocks/worlds/`) also ignore themselves. A `.gitignore` can't untrack a file git already tracks; if you committed one earlier, run `git rm --cached `. ## Good to know **Build path.** For new landing pages and showcase surfaces, Impeccable can generate a full-fidelity comp first and build to match it (bolder, slower), or build straight in code (leaner, faster). App screens and documents are always built in code. `init` asks once and saves the answer as `buildPath` in `.impeccable/config.json`; the decision page lets you override it for one session. The choice only appears when your harness can generate images. [Image generation](https://impeccable.style/docs/image-generation) · [Configuration](https://impeccable.style/docs/config). **Hooks run outside model approval.** In Claude Code, installed command hooks run even when you deny the model's own commands, so the first edit can download the engine. Review installed hooks before unattended runs, or pass `--settings '{"disableAllHooks": true}'` to turn them off for a run. The installer leaves hook entries it didn't add alone. **Something broken?** `/impeccable doctor` finds stale context files, unused settings, and broken hooks. [Fix setup problems](https://impeccable.style/docs/doctor). **Telemetry.** When a new design starts, the skill fetches a set of visual directions from the impeccable.style catalog. Turning telemetry off doesn't stop that request; it stops the anonymous record of which directions were shown and which one you picked, which is how the catalog learns what works. Your project name, files, code, and `PRODUCT.md` are never sent. Disable telemetry with `npx impeccable telemetry off`, `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`, or `"telemetry": false` in `.impeccable/config.json` for the whole project. The full list of what is sent is on the [privacy page](https://impeccable.style/privacy). ## Community - [Issues](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/issues) for bugs, questions, and ideas. Outside contributions start with an issue; see [DEVELOP.md](docs/DEVELOP.md). - [Changelog](https://impeccable.style/changelog) for what shipped. - Follow [@pbakaus](https://x.com/pbakaus) for release notes and new rules. ## License Apache 2.0. --- ## Supported hosts **1.1.81 and newer target DSH 0.2.1-rc.2.** 0.2.0 still works. Do not apply it to 0.1.x. - **dsh 0.2.1-rc.2** (official desktop / official `dsh web`): use **1.1.81** or newer. Fixes `{{cwd}}` / `[cwd]` crash, patch #40 match, dropped `toolFilter`, host `dsh-tools` resolve, hostFs fd, desktop helper self-kill, `file:` archive update, Ctrl+Enter steer. - **dsh 0.2.0-rc.2**: use **1.1.40** or newer; this line also installs. - **dsh 0.1.7** (incl. rc.1 / rc.2): use **1.1.39** or older — pick the tag on [Releases](https://github.com/HunYiSage/dsh-purge/releases). - **dsh 0.2.1-rc.3 / rc.4 and newer are not supported.** Unmatched patches stay pending or skipped; nothing is rewritten blindly. Stay on **0.2.1-rc.2**. Unmatched patches stay pending or skipped; nothing is rewritten blindly. --- ## Install **Do not use the plugin marketplace.** One-click install on [dsh-plugin.org](https://dsh-plugin.org) or in Settings → Plugin Market fails with `already queued: dsh-purge` and never runs a command. The name is not on the npm registry, so do not `pnpm add dsh-purge`. ### Quick start Have `dsh` on PATH? One command, one restart, one click. Run the line for the host you open (the desktop EXE is the same with `desktop` instead of `web`): ```sh # Official `dsh web` dsh plugin --profile web add https://codeload.github.com/HunYiSage/dsh-purge/tar.gz/refs/heads/master # Official desktop EXE dsh plugin --profile desktop add https://codeload.github.com/HunYiSage/dsh-purge/tar.gz/refs/heads/master ``` 1. **Fully quit and reopen** the host you installed into. Web: stop `dsh web` and start it again. Desktop: quit the tray icon too, then open the exe. 2. On that host, click **dsh-purge** beside the session title → **Clean** → **Apply**. A successful Apply restarts the host once. Done — verify with `/purge status` in chat. If pnpm asks about build scripts, or anything below does not appear, follow the step by step. ### Step by step **Step 1 — Pick your host.** Official `dsh web` and the official desktop EXE are installed and patched **separately**; only install into the host you actually open. | What you run | Profile | Install command | |---|---|---| | Official `dsh web` | `web` | the `web` line in Quick start | | Official desktop EXE | `desktop` | the `desktop` line in Quick start | **Step 2 — Install the plugin.** Use the `codeload.github.com` URL exactly. Do not use `github.com/.../archive`: that 302 makes pnpm fail with `fetch failed`. Have `dsh`? Run the Quick start line for your profile. If this directory is already a clone, use `.` instead of the URL. pnpm only (no `dsh` required): run this inside the profile you actually use, not the repo root. ```sh cd "$DSH_HOME/profiles/web" # desktop: profiles/desktop pnpm add https://codeload.github.com/HunYiSage/dsh-purge/tar.gz/refs/heads/master ``` Windows PowerShell: ```powershell cd "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\profiles\web" # desktop: profiles\desktop pnpm add https://codeload.github.com/HunYiSage/dsh-purge/tar.gz/refs/heads/master ``` `pnpm add` and `dsh plugin add` fetch the package; `postinstall` writes `dsh-purge` into `dsh.profile.bundles` and adds a body `insert` in the profile `cordis.patch.yml`. Without that insert the host never loads the plugin and no button appears. **Expected result:** `node_modules/dsh-purge/package.json` exists, `"dsh-purge"` is in that profile's `bundles`, and `cordis.patch.yml` has an `id: dsh-purge` insert. - pnpm 11/12 skips install scripts (`ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS`) unless you allow the build: ```sh pnpm add --allow-build=dsh-purge --allow-build=dsh-purge@https://codeload.github.com/HunYiSage/dsh-purge/tar.gz/refs/heads/master https://codeload.github.com/HunYiSage/dsh-purge/tar.gz/refs/heads/master # Already installed, warning only — the full specifier is required (name-only leaves "set this to true or false"): pnpm approve-builds dsh-purge@https://codeload.github.com/HunYiSage/dsh-purge/tar.gz/refs/heads/master # If bundles / insert are still missing: node node_modules/dsh-purge/scripts/ensure-profile-bundle.mjs ``` - If neither `dsh` nor pnpm is available, jump to [Manual install](#manual). - On the desktop client you can also click the button (`dsh://` deep link; it still downloads the same tarball).

Install in desktop client

**Step 3 — Restart the host.** Adding the plugin to a profile does **not** patch `@deepseek-ai` by itself. Fully quit and reopen the host you just installed into (Web: stop `dsh web` and start again; Desktop: quit the tray icon too, then open the exe). **Expected result:** **dsh-purge** stands beside the session title. Missing? Jump to Step 5. **Step 4 — Apply and verify.** On **that host**, click **dsh-purge** beside the session title, open **Clean**, and click **Apply**. It is not on the host Settings page. A successful **Apply** restarts once; it does not restart if it did not finish. Web controls affect Web only; desktop controls affect the desktop app only. Do not Apply one host from the other. **Expected result:** `/purge status` in chat prints `DSH_HOME` and the patch list — the path should be the home you actually run. Optional packages that are not installed (liangshen) show as skipped and do not block Apply. **Step 5 — Troubleshooting.** Jump here only when a step above did not end with its expected result. - **No button beside the session title.** Run `dsh --dump-config` (or `dsh --profile desktop --dump-config`) and look for a body row `id: dsh-purge` (not `dsh-purge-redteam`). If it is absent, run `ensure-profile-bundle.mjs` (Step 2), then fully quit and reopen the host. After this version, a live red-team child entry also writes the missing insert on startup — quit and reopen once more. `entry "redteam-store" not found` at the top is leftover from an old red-team package and can be ignored. - **The market says `already queued: dsh-purge`.** Stop clicking the market; use `dsh plugin add` or pnpm from Step 2. If the CLI also says it is already there, remove and re-add, then redo Step 3: ```sh dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-purge dsh plugin --profile desktop add https://codeload.github.com/HunYiSage/dsh-purge/tar.gz/refs/heads/master ``` pnpm only: ```sh cd "$DSH_HOME/profiles/desktop" pnpm remove dsh-purge pnpm add https://codeload.github.com/HunYiSage/dsh-purge/tar.gz/refs/heads/master ``` Swap `desktop` for `web` on Web. ### Advanced **Hand this to an assistant.** Paste the block below to a local assistant. It should only run the install command — no disk scan, no other edits, no Apply, no restart.
For AI assistants (install only) Install the DeepSeek Harness plugin `dsh-purge` into the Web profile only. Do not scan the whole disk, do not read or edit other files, do not apply settings, and do not restart the app. Do not install into the desktop profile. Do not use the plugin marketplace. The name is not on the npm registry; do not `pnpm add dsh-purge`. **Web (official `dsh web`)** If `dsh` is on PATH: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add https://codeload.github.com/HunYiSage/dsh-purge/tar.gz/refs/heads/master ``` If `dsh` is missing and pnpm is available, `cd` into `$DSH_HOME/profiles/web` (often `~/.dsh/profiles/web`) and run: ```sh pnpm add https://codeload.github.com/HunYiSage/dsh-purge/tar.gz/refs/heads/master ``` If this directory is already a clone and `dsh` exists, use `dsh plugin --profile web add .`. If neither `dsh` nor pnpm is available, tell the user and stop. After the command finishes, tell the user to fully quit and restart `dsh web`, then open **dsh-purge** beside the session title and **Apply** on **Clean**. Then stop.
**Manual install.** Use this when the command fails or `dsh` is not on PATH. Edit **only the profile for the host you run** — do not touch the other, and do not delete existing bundles.
Full manual steps **1. Find the `$DSH_HOME` this host uses.** A real home is named `.dsh` (official EXE sometimes `dsh-home`), contains `profiles`, and has at least one `profiles//package.json`. Check in order: `DSH_HOME` env → `.dsh` next to the install root (portable) → `%USERPROFILE%\.dsh` or `~/.dsh` → `%APPDATA%` / `%LOCALAPPDATA%\DeepSeek Harness\dsh-home`. Confirm: `profiles/web/package.json` has `"name": "dsh-profile-web"` (or `dsh-profile-desktop`). Machines often have two homes — use the one that belongs to the host you actually start. PowerShell to list candidates: ```powershell $cands = @() if ($env:DSH_HOME) { $cands += $env:DSH_HOME } $cands += "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh" $dsh = Get-Command dsh -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue if ($dsh) { $dir = Split-Path $dsh.Source $cands += @((Join-Path $dir ".dsh"), (Join-Path (Split-Path $dir) ".dsh"), (Join-Path (Split-Path (Split-Path $dir)) ".dsh")) } $cands += @("$env:APPDATA\DeepSeek Harness\dsh-home", "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\DeepSeek Harness\dsh-home") $cands | Select-Object -Unique | Where-Object { $_ -and (Test-Path (Join-Path $_ "profiles")) } ``` **2. Put the plugin at `$DSH_HOME/plugins/dsh-purge`** (folder must be named `dsh-purge`, with a `package.json` whose `"name"` is `dsh-purge`). ```sh git clone https://github.com/HunYiSage/dsh-purge.git "$DSH_HOME/plugins/dsh-purge" ``` Without git: download [master.tar.gz](https://github.com/HunYiSage/dsh-purge/archive/refs/heads/master.tar.gz), extract, rename `dsh-purge-master` → `dsh-purge`, and place it under `plugins`. If you already have a clone, copy the whole tree — not a few `.js` files. **3. Edit only that profile's `package.json` — back it up first.** Web → `$DSH_HOME/profiles/web/package.json`; desktop → `$DSH_HOME/profiles/desktop/package.json`. Add **only two things**, keeping every existing dependency and bundle: 1. In `dependencies`, add `"dsh-purge": "file:../../plugins/dsh-purge"` 2. At the **end** of `dsh.profile.bundles`, append `"dsh-purge"` (skip if already there) ```json { "name": "dsh-profile-web", "private": true, "dependencies": { "dsh-purge": "file:../../plugins/dsh-purge" }, "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": [ "@deepseek-ai/dsh-base", "@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app", "dsh-purge" ], "patchReload": "live" } } } ``` Keep JSON valid (comma before the new item, none after the last). Do not switch `file:../../plugins/dsh-purge` to an absolute path, do not touch `patchReload` or other plugins, and do not list `"dsh-purge"` twice. On desktop, if there is no `dsh-web-app` row, do not add one. **4. Run `pnpm install` in that profile only** (`cd` into the profile dir, not the repo root or `$DSH_HOME`): ```sh cd "$DSH_HOME/profiles/web" # or profiles/desktop pnpm install ``` Success: `profiles//node_modules/dsh-purge/package.json` exists. If `pnpm` is missing, use the Node / pnpm shipped with official `dsh`; on `Could not resolve`, re-check the `file:` path; on a JSON error, fix commas or restore the backup. **5. Fully quit that host, reopen it, then Apply** — Step 3 and Step 4 above. The card appears beside the session title; click **Apply** (or `/purge apply`) on that host only. If the card is missing, you likely edited the other `.dsh` — go back to step 1.
**Uninstall.** **dsh-purge** beside the session title → **Clean** → **Uninstall**. Confirm the dialog: it reverts any applied patches, restores the original Harness, and restarts the current host. Disable or uninstall also resets an agent-preset default that still points at `redteam` back to `standard`, so the host can create sessions after the preset is gone.
Uninstall commands and config ```sh # or from a terminal / chat dsh-purge --uninstall # /purge uninstall ``` Plugin config lives in `cordis.patch.yml` (`postPrompt` is empty by default): ```yaml - insert: - id: dsh-purge name: 'dsh-purge' config: enabled: true autoApplyOnStart: true autoUpdateOnStart: false autoRevertOnMissing: false verbose: false postPromptOrder: 5100 postPrompt: "" ```
--- ## Preview **dsh-purge** sits beside the session title. It opens a right-hand dock with two pages: **Clean** and **Drill**. Switch **Light / Ink**. Patches are grouped; the count only includes items that actually applied. Rule sets sit in a list above the editor, with Enable and Delete on each row. The first time you open Drill you read the notice, wait out the countdown, scroll to the end, and check three boxes. Clean does not need that step. Drill is only for a host you manage, an offline target, or an exercise that already has written authorization. **Clean** ![Clean](docs/preview/dock-clean.png) **Drill authorization** ![Drill authorization](docs/preview/dock-auth.png) **Drill** ![Drill](docs/preview/dock-drill.png) **Patches** ![Patches](docs/preview/settings.png) **Local lab** Penetration, attack, or scanning against mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau, banks and financial sites, government and military sites is prohibited. | Area | What it shows | |---|---| | dsh-purge | button beside the session title; opens or collapses the dock | | Clean | patches, prompt, rule sets | | Drill | assets and environment after authorization. The skill library and knowledge base ship with it. The tab says Unauthorized until then | | Patches | grouped status, Apply, Restore, or Uninstall | | Prompt | edit `prompt-inject.md` as the session override | | Local lab | penetration of mainland China / Hong Kong / Macau, banks, government and military sites is prohibited | | Rule sets | multiple `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`; Enable writes under `$DSH_HOME`, Delete removes the row | --- ## Layout `bin/` is the CLI, `lib/` is patches and the drill console, `presets/redteam/` is the red-team preset, `skills/redteam/` holds the bundled skills, and `client.js` is the dock. Runtime files live under `$DSH_HOME`: `prompt-inject.md`, `rules/`, `skills/`, `redteam/`. If `DSH_HOME` is unset, the launcher-adjacent `.dsh` wins over `~/.dsh`. Web and the desktop app each use their own home. --- ## Usage ```sh dsh-purge --status dsh-purge --apply dsh-purge --revert dsh-purge --uninstall dsh-purge --edit /purge status | apply | revert | uninstall | edit | help /rules list | use | create | delete | reset | help /rewind # If another plugin already owns /rewind (or /purge, /rules, /skills), that # name is skipped or remounted as /purge-rewind. Other commands, tools, and # /dsh-purge/* routes keep working. purge_status purge_apply purge_revert ``` After a successful Apply, the host restarts so patched packages load; you can also click **Restart** manually. Under the patch title are the stable release and the test release. The test release follows the `beta` branch. **Switch to stable** installs `master` and clears any pin. Picking an older stable version pins it; click **Update** to return to the latest. Old test tags are not listed. The composer **Undo once** and **Undo last round** stay in the current conversation and do not open a branch. The sent line goes back into the input, and that cut's already-sent messages and completed tasks leave the current conversation; edit and **send again**. From **1.1.61**, rewind bounds follow the **current turn**, not the first user message. `/rewind` does the same. If the **same task works in standard but fails in minimal or PTC**, preset `run_code`, sandbox, or plan intercept text is often still uncleared, or built-in minimal is missing `agent-instructions`. Use **1.1.61+**, then **quit the host fully → Apply in Clean → restart → start a new chat**. Switching preset alone does not reload patches in the running process. ### Response speed DSH runs Bash calls in a tool batch one at a time. Older dsh-purge releases raised the default foreground wait from 60 seconds to 10 minutes, so one slow command could hold up later calls for that long. Patch #21 now restores marked plugin values to the official 60-second default. Unmarked timeouts and other custom values are preserved; an unmarked 10-minute value cannot reliably be distinguished from a user setting. For a shorter wait in `dsh web` on macOS/Linux, add this entry to `$DSH_HOME/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` (normally `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`). Edit an existing entry with the same id instead of adding a duplicate. This profile layer is applied after the bundled configuration, so future plugin applies keep the override. ```yaml - id: bash-sandbox config: timeoutMs: 10000 ``` With the standard jobs service and `promoteOnTimeout: true`, an unfinished command returns a background job id after 10 seconds and keeps running. Read it with `job_output` or stop it with `job_kill`. This changes the foreground wait, not the command's speed. Without that service or with promotion disabled, the timeout kills the command. A per-call `timeoutMs` overrides this default; `run_in_background: true` returns a job id immediately. For routine tasks, you can also opt into Low reasoning for new sessions: ```yaml - id: agent-default-model config: provider: deepseek-official model: deepseek-flash reasoningEffort: low ``` Restart `dsh web` to load the profile. The model and reasoning defaults apply to newly created sessions; select Low in the composer for an existing session. The plugin does not change these model preferences automatically. Keep High when the task needs deeper reasoning, and narrow file searches rather than recursively scanning every application directory. ### Local lab Penetration, attack, or scanning against mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau, banks and financial sites, government and military sites is prohibited. --- ## Local checks ```sh node --check lib/index.js node --check lib/core.js node --check lib/surface.js node --check lib/web.js node --check lib/desktop.js node --check lib/host.js node --check lib/rewind.js node --check lib/skills.js node --check client.js ``` --- ## How it works Apply, on start or when you click Apply: ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Start or click Apply"] --> B{"Patch already in place?"} B -->|yes| C["Skip"] B -->|no| D["Back up the original as .dshpurge.bak"] D --> E["Replace the matched files"] E --> F["Override the shim"] F --> G["Inject the encrypted prompt shipped in the plugin, the text the prompt box shows by default"] ``` Override on each session: ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Restart or new session"] --> B["Inject the plugin's encrypted default. No save click, and no host prompt file"] ``` Prompt injection and ruleset decision at every turn. The three inputs on the left are what you control in the dsh-purge panel; the dotted edges show which decision each one drives: ```mermaid flowchart TD L["Rule library: activate a set → writes prompt-inject.md"] W["Local rules: check AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md in the current dir"] P["Workspace policy: strict / fallback / always"] A["Turn start"] --> B{"prompt-inject.md non-empty?"} B -->|yes| C["Inject = prompt-inject.md (A)"] B -->|no| D{"Any checked local md in the current dir, non-empty?"} D -->|yes| E["Inject = selected workspace md (B)"] D -->|no| F["Inject = plugin encrypted slot default (D)"] C --> G{"Workspace baseline policy (C)"} E --> G F --> G G -->|strict| H["Drop DSH workspace baseline section"] G -->|fallback default| I{"User inject present above? (A or B)"} G -->|always| J["Keep DSH workspace baseline section"] I -->|yes| H I -->|no| J H --> K["Final system prompt"] J --> K L -.-> B W -.-> D P -.-> G ``` --- ## Restore - Each target is copied to `.dshpurge.bak` before the first apply. - **Restore** or `/purge revert` copies backups back and deletes them. With no backup, shim lines written by this plugin are stripped. - `prompt-inject.md` is a user file and is kept. - **Uninstall** restores first if patches were applied, then deletes the inject file, rule library, and the plugin itself. - Apply is idempotent. --- ## Path detection The host surface is detected first: `web` / `desktop` (`gui` / `tui` are reserved and still fall back to web). **Web:** 1. `DSH_HOME` / `DSH_BASE` 2. `.dsh` next to the dsh launcher (portable install, any drive) 3. `npm prefix -g` / `npm root -g` 4. Nested `@deepseek-ai/dsh/node_modules/@deepseek-ai` 5. `~/.dsh` **Official desktop EXE:** the running official Harness install (`resources/app` or the unpacked package). The drive letter is not hard-coded. A successful Apply restarts once. Community Desktop is not maintained. Official npm-global is not patched. Sealed `host-commands` / `runtime-commands` are scrubbed, never injected. If nothing is found, set `DSH_BASE` / `DSH_DESKTOP_INSTALL`. No files are changed. --- ## Releases Team channel: [t.me/LLM_PoJia](https://t.me/LLM_PoJia), used for announcements and updates. GitHub [Releases](https://github.com/HunYiSage/dsh-purge/releases) still hosts older packages. Resale of the original build is prohibited; forks must attribute, and third-party builds are not affiliated with the original author or this team. ## Notes - Scope is rendered copy, defaults, and runtime logic inside local `@deepseek-ai/*` packages, plus override files and rule sets under the harness home. - After an upgrade, unmatched originals show as skipped. Apply still completes, and those files are left unchanged. - Third-party plugin *source repos* outside `@deepseek-ai` are left alone (CMD silence may **best-effort** patch installed doctor / market / liangshen / mnemon at runtime). - Install from the GitHub tarball (the name is not on npm; skip the plugin market). With `dsh`: `dsh plugin --profile web add https://codeload.github.com/HunYiSage/dsh-purge/tar.gz/refs/heads/master`. pnpm only: `pnpm add` that URL inside `$DSH_HOME/profiles/web`. Use `desktop` for the EXE. From this repo, `add .`. --- Thanks to the [LINUX DO](https://linux.do) community

repositories.name: floci
repositories.description: Light, fluffy, and always free - The AWS Local Emulator alternative
repositories.readme:
Any Cloud. Locally.
Light, fluffy, and always free
No account. No auth token. No feature gates. Just docker compose up.

Quick Start · Features · Services · SDKs · Testcontainers · Migration · Docs

--- ## What is Floci? Floci is a free, open-source local AWS emulator for development, testing, and CI. It gives you AWS-shaped services on your machine without requiring a cloud account, an auth token, or paid feature gates. Point your AWS SDK, CLI, Terraform, CDK, OpenTofu, or test suite at `http://localhost:4566` and keep your existing workflows. Already using LocalStack? Floci is a drop-in replacement: swap the image and keep going. See [Migrating from LocalStack](#migrating-from-localstack). Floci is the AWS member of the [Floci](https://github.com/floci-io) emulator family, named after [floccus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cirrocumulus_floccus), the cloud formation that looks like popcorn. | Emulator | Cloud | Port | |---|---|:---:| | **[floci](https://github.com/floci-io/floci)** | **AWS** | **4566** | | [floci-az](https://github.com/floci-io/floci-az) | Azure | 4577 | | [floci-gcp](https://github.com/floci-io/floci-gcp) | GCP | 4588 | | [floci-oci](https://github.com/floci-io/floci-oci) | OCI | 4599 | ## Quick Start The fastest way to run Floci is with the official [CLI](https://github.com/floci-io/floci-cli) ```bash floci start ``` No Docker? Each [release](https://github.com/floci-io/floci/releases) also ships a standalone `floci-aws` binary for Linux, macOS and Windows; see [Native binary](https://floci.io/floci/getting-started/installation/#native-binary). Export the AWS environment variables: ```bash eval $(floci env) ``` Use your existing AWS tools normally: ```bash aws s3 mb s3://my-bucket aws dynamodb create-table \ --table-name demo-table \ --attribute-definitions AttributeName=pk,AttributeType=S \ --key-schema AttributeName=pk,KeyType=HASH \ --billing-mode PAY_PER_REQUEST aws dynamodb list-tables ``` ### Watch it run This short demo shows the CLI flow: start Floci, export the local AWS environment, run standard AWS CLI commands, and stop the emulator. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b55714dc-ef36-40ae-a734-cd2cadc288a8 All AWS services are available at `http://localhost:4566`. Any [published AWS region](https://floci.io/floci/configuration/partitions/) works, in every partition. Credentials can be any non-empty values unless you explicitly enable stricter service-specific auth checks.
Prefer Docker Compose? Create a `compose.yaml` file: ```yaml services: floci: image: floci/floci:latest ports: - "4566:4566" ``` Start Floci: ```bash docker compose up ``` Then configure your AWS environment manually: ```bash export AWS_ENDPOINT_URL=http://localhost:4566 export AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-1 export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=test export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=test ```
Using the old hectorvent/floci image? Update your image name: ```yaml # Before image: hectorvent/floci:latest # After image: floci/floci:latest ``` The old `hectorvent/floci` repository no longer receives updates.
## Web Console Floci ships a browser console for inspecting the resources in your local emulator. **Open it at:** `http://localhost:4566/_floci/ui` Nothing runs at boot. The first request pulls the console image, starts it as a sidecar container on Floci's Docker network, hands it Floci's own reachable address plus the standard AWS environment, polls its health endpoint, and redirects the browser once it reports it can reach Floci. The sidecar's port is bound by Docker, so it needs no `ports:` entry of your own, and its logs are streamed into CloudWatch Logs under `/floci/ui`. Starting a container needs the Docker socket: ```yaml services: floci: image: floci/floci:latest ports: - "4566:4566" volumes: - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock ``` | Variable | Default | Description | |---|---|---| | `FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_ENABLED` | `true` | Enable the console sidecar | | `FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_IMAGE` | `floci/floci-ui:0.7.0` | Console image to run | | `FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_CONTAINER_NAME` | `floci-ui` | Name of the sidecar container | | `FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_PORT` | `4500` | Host port the console is published on | | `FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_BIND_ADDRESS` | _(none)_ | Host interface that port is published on. Unset publishes on every interface; set `127.0.0.1` when Floci's own port is loopback-only | | `FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_KEEP_RUNNING_ON_SHUTDOWN` | `false` | Leave the sidecar running when Floci stops | ### Running a different console The console is not fixed to the one Floci ships. Any console implementing the [Floci console contract](https://floci.io/floci/ui/console-contract/) runs with nothing but an image name: listen on the port in `PORT`, serve `GET /api/health`, talk to Floci at `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`. ```yaml environment: FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_IMAGE: acme/my-console:1.0 ``` A console that differs from the contract's defaults says so in its own `io.floci.console.*` image labels, so its operators do not have to. [StackPort](https://github.com/DaviReisVieira/stackport), for example, listens on 8080 rather than 4500; on an image that predates the labels, say it by hand: ```yaml environment: FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_IMAGE: davireis/stackport:latest FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_CONTAINER_NAME: floci-stackport FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_PORT: "8080" FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_INTERNAL_PORT: "8080" ``` [Floci Dash](https://github.com/ofsazib/floci-dash) is another. It honours `PORT`, so only the two things it does differ on need naming: ```yaml environment: FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_IMAGE: ghcr.io/ofsazib/floci-dash:latest FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_CONTAINER_NAME: floci-dash FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_ENDPOINT_ENV: FLOCI_URL FLOCI_SERVICES_UI_STATUS_PATH: /api/healthz ``` The endpoint itself is never configured by hand: Floci resolves its own reachable address at start time and injects it as `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`. Full reference: [Web Console](https://floci.io/floci/ui/) and [Console Contract v1](https://floci.io/floci/ui/console-contract/). ## Features
Local AWS without the cloud account Run AWS-compatible services locally without an AWS account, auth token, or paid feature gates.
Real Docker where fidelity matters Lambda, RDS, Neptune, ElastiCache, MSK, ECS, EC2, EKS, OpenSearch, CodeBuild, and Managed Service for Apache Flink use real Docker-backed execution instead of shallow mocks.
Drop-in AWS compatibility Point standard AWS clients at `http://localhost:4566`. Existing credentials, regions, SDKs, CLI commands, and IaC workflows stay familiar. Terraform can provision AWS-shaped resources locally through Floci using the standard HashiCorp AWS provider. See the [Terraform with Floci guide](docs/getting-started/terraform.md) for provider configuration, resource examples, and optional emulated S3 state.
Fast enough for CI The native image starts in milliseconds and keeps idle memory low, making it practical for local development and test pipelines.
Configurable persistence Choose from in-memory, persistent, hybrid, and write-ahead log storage depending on the durability profile you need.
## Why Floci? LocalStack's community edition [sunset in March 2026](https://blog.localstack.cloud/the-road-ahead-for-localstack/), requiring auth tokens and freezing security updates. Floci is the no-strings-attached alternative. | Capability | Floci | LocalStack Community | |---|:---:|:---:| | Auth token required | No | Yes | | Security updates | Yes | Frozen | | Startup time | ~24 ms | ~3.3 s | | Idle memory | ~13 MiB | ~143 MiB | | Docker image size | ~90 MB | ~1.0 GB | | License | MIT | Restricted | | API Gateway v2 / HTTP API | Yes | No | | Cognito | Yes | No | | RDS, ElastiCache, MSK | Real Docker | No | | Neptune (graph DB + Gremlin WebSocket) | Real Docker | No | | DocumentDB (MongoDB-compatible) | Real Docker | No | | ECS, EC2, EKS | Real Docker | No | | CodeBuild | Real Docker execution | No | | Native binary | ~40 MB | No | **Broad AWS coverage. Free forever.** See the [Services Overview](https://floci.io/floci/services/) for the full list of emulated services. ## Architecture Overview ```mermaid flowchart LR Client["AWS SDK / CLI"] subgraph Floci ["Floci, port 4566"] Router["HTTP Router\nJAX-RS / Vert.x"] subgraph Stateless ["Stateless Services"] A["SSM · SQS · SNS\nIAM · STS · KMS\nSecrets Manager · SES\nCognito · Kinesis\nEventBridge · Scheduler · AppConfig\nCloudWatch · Step Functions\nCloudFormation · ACM · Config · CloudTrail\nAPI Gateway · AppSync · ELB v2 · Auto Scaling\nElastic Beanstalk · CodeDeploy · CodePipeline · Backup · FIS · Bedrock Runtime · Bedrock AgentCore · Route53 · Transfer"] end subgraph Stateful ["Stateful Services"] B["S3 · DynamoDB\nDynamoDB Streams"] end subgraph Containers ["Container Services"] C["Lambda\nElastiCache\nRDS\nNeptune\nECS\nEC2\nMSK\nEKS\nOpenSearch\nCodeBuild\nManaged Flink"] D["Athena -> floci-duck\nDuckDB sidecar"] end Router --> Stateless Router --> Stateful Router --> Containers Stateless & Stateful --> Store[("StorageBackend\nmemory · hybrid · persistent · wal")] end Docker["Docker Engine"] Client -->|"HTTP :4566\nAWS wire protocol"| Router Containers -->|"Docker API\nIAM / SigV4 auth"| Docker ``` ## Supported Services Floci supports local emulation for application services, data services, eventing, identity, infrastructure, billing, and container-backed workloads. | Category | Services | |---|---| | Core app services | S3, SQS, SNS, DynamoDB, Lambda, Lambda MicroVMs, Lambda Web Functions, IAM, STS, KMS, Payment Cryptography, Secrets Manager, SSM | | Events and workflows | EventBridge, EventBridge V2, EventBridge Pipes, EventBridge Scheduler, Step Functions, SWF, CloudWatch Logs, CloudWatch Metrics, CloudWatch OAM, CloudWatch RUM, Managed Prometheus (AMP) | | API and identity | API Gateway REST, API Gateway v2, AppSync, Cognito, Cognito Identity, ACM, Route53, Route 53 Resolver, Cloud Map, Global Accelerator | | Containers and compute | ECS, EC2, Lightsail, EKS, MWAA, ECR, EFS, CodeBuild, CodeDeploy, CodePipeline, CodeGuru Reviewer, CodeArtifact, AWS Batch, Auto Scaling, Application Auto Scaling, Elastic Beanstalk, ELB v2, ELB Classic | | Data, analytics, and AI | Athena, Glue, Lake Formation, EMR, EMR Serverless, Redshift, Redshift Data API, Redshift Serverless, Firehose, Managed Service for Apache Flink, OpenSearch, S3 Tables, S3 Vectors, Textract, Transcribe, Comprehend, Rekognition, Translate, Bedrock, Bedrock Runtime, Bedrock AgentCore, Bedrock AgentCore Control, SageMaker | | Databases and caching | Aurora DSQL, RDS, RDS Data API, Neptune, DocumentDB, DMS, MemoryDB, ElastiCache, Timestream for InfluxDB | | Messaging and transfer | SES, Kinesis, MSK, Amazon MQ, Transfer Family, DataSync, IoT Core, Amazon Connect, Amazon AppIntegrations | | Security and governance | AWS Network Firewall, AWS RAM, Service Quotas, WAF v2, GuardDuty, Amazon Inspector, CloudTrail, CloudFront, Resource Groups Tagging API, Resource Explorer 2, CloudHSM v2, Organizations, AWS Account Management, IAM Access Analyzer, IAM Identity Center (SSO Admin, OIDC, Access Portal, SCIM), Identity Store, Amazon Macie, Amazon Detective, Security Hub, Amazon Verified Permissions, Control Catalog, Control Tower, Service Catalog, AWS Marketplace | | Cost and billing | AWS Budgets, Pricing, Cost Explorer, Cost and Usage Reports, BCM Pricing Calculator, BCM Data Exports | | Resilience, backup, and config | AWS FIS, AWS Backup, Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager, AWS Config, AppConfig, AppConfigData, CloudFormation, Cloud Control API | For operation-level compatibility, see the [Services Overview](https://floci.io/floci/services/).
Detailed service notes | Service | How it works | Notable features | |---|---|---| | SSM | In-process + EC2 containers | Parameter Store (version history, labels, SecureString, tagging); Run Command (SendCommand, GetCommandInvocation, direct EC2 container execution, agent polling) | | SQS | In-process | Standard and FIFO queues, DLQ, visibility timeout, batch operations, tagging | | SNS | In-process | Topics, subscriptions, SQS, Lambda and HTTP delivery, tagging | | S3 | In-process | Versioning, multipart upload, pre-signed URLs, Object Lock, object annotations, event notifications | | S3 Vectors | In-process | Vector buckets, indexes, put / get / list / delete vectors, cosine similarity queries | | DynamoDB | In-process | GSI, LSI, Query, Scan, TTL, transactions, batch operations; Streams with shard iterators and Lambda event source mapping | | Lambda | Real Docker | Runtime environment, execution model, warm container pool, aliases, Function URLs | | API Gateway REST | In-process | Resources, methods, stages, Lambda proxy, MOCK integrations, AWS integrations | | API Gateway v2 | In-process | HTTP APIs, routes, integrations, JWT authorizers, stages | | AppSync | In-process | GraphQL API management API, schema registry, AWS scalars, domain names, channel namespaces | | IAM | In-process | Users, roles, groups, policies, instance profiles, access keys; STS AssumeRole, WebIdentity, SAML, GetFederationToken, GetSessionToken | | Cognito | In-process | User pools, app clients, auth flows, JWKS and OpenID well-known endpoints | | KMS | In-process | Encrypt, decrypt, sign, verify, data keys, aliases | | Payment Cryptography | In-process | Keys with real AES-256 material and check values, aliases, tagging | | Kinesis | In-process | Streams, shards, enhanced fan-out, split and merge | | Secrets Manager | In-process | Versioning, resource policies, tagging | | Step Functions | In-process | ASL execution, task tokens, execution history | | SWF | In-process | Decision and activity tasks, timers, child workflows, timeouts, real Lambda invocation | | CloudFormation | In-process | Stacks, change sets, resource provisioning, StackSets (cross-account instances) | | EventBridge | In-process | Custom buses, rules, SQS, SNS and Lambda targets | | EventBridge V2 | In-process | Event buses and filtered subscribers delivering to SQS | | EventBridge Pipes | In-process | Poller-based integration connecting SQS, Kinesis, DynamoDB, and MSK sources to targets with optional filtering | | EventBridge Scheduler | In-process | Schedule groups, schedules, flexible time windows, retry policies, DLQs | | CloudWatch Logs | In-process | Log groups, streams, ingestion, filtering | | CloudWatch Metrics | In-process | Custom metrics, statistics, alarms | | CloudWatch OAM | In-process | Full 15-operation sink, policy, cross-account link, and tagging API | | ElastiCache | Real Docker | Redis / Valkey protocol, IAM auth, SigV4 validation | | MemoryDB | Real Docker | Redis / Valkey protocol via real containers; JSON 1.1 control plane; reuses ElastiCache RESP proxy | | Aurora DSQL | Real Docker, mock mode available | PostgreSQL 16 per cluster behind a TLS endpoint with IAM token auth, `AWS IAM GRANT` role mappings; not yet DSQL's limits and async indexes | | RDS | Real Docker | PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, IAM auth, JDBC-compatible engines | | Timestream for InfluxDB | Real Docker, mock mode available | InfluxDB 2.x DB instances and read replica clusters via `influxdb:2.7`; initial auth secret in Secrets Manager; backups and restore through the influx CLI | | RDS Data API | REST JSON over real RDS containers | Raw SQL execution and transactions for local MySQL / MariaDB RDS resources | | Neptune | Real Docker | Graph DB via TinkerPop Gremlin Server (default) or Neo4j for openCypher/Bolt (`NEPTUNE_DB_TYPE`);
